business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Independent, client-first wealth manager focused on financial wellbeing", headquartered in Ahmedabad, Gujarat with presence in Surat, Pune and Mumbai; "Over three decades of trusted wealth management expertise" and the "First independent advisor listed on the NSE and now listed on BSE also".
- Ranked "33rd Rank in India - MF Distribution", footnoted as "*Based on revenue data as per latest available AMFI report" (data as on June 2026).
- USP framed as Direct-to-Client ("No intermediaries, 100% aligned"), Vendor-Agnostic ("Unbiased, independent advice"), Personalised Strategies, Simplicity & Integrity, Client Empowerment, Transparent Engagement and Capital Protection ("Risk-managed, fixed income roots").
- Culture described as "Education over persuasion. Relationships over transactions. Trust over targets.", with a "Referral-led growth model built on credibility" and a "Target-free culture" for Relationship Managers.
- Concentration acknowledged: "~70% of client base from Gujarat - our cornerstone", with a "Strong base in Ahmedabad; expanding to Pune & Surat".

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- Trading book deliberately wound down: "the Company has consciously reduced its trading book to nil as part of its strategy to focus on its core businesses" (Q1 FY26 had included Rs 9 Cr of revenue from trading activity).
- Growth is being funded through deployment into new platforms - ~Rs 41 Cr into the Lakshya AMC JV and Rs 52.1 Cr for the 51% WFA stake - with the deck attributing higher employee and other expenses to "the ongoing build-out of the AMC and Insurance Broking businesses".
- WFA is structured as a "Share-swap transaction: Promoter Mr. Ashish Shah will remain invested in the combined entity, reflecting confidence in its long-term growth", with "Leadership continuity: Key talent and relationship managers to be retained".
- The historical consolidated balance sheet shows no borrowings at Mar-26, Mar-25 and Mar-24 (Rs 0.04 Cr at Mar-23), total equity of Rs 170.1 Cr at Mar-26 (including Non Controlling Interest of Rs 19.6 Cr, first appearing in Mar-26), and non-current Investments rising to Rs 105.5 Cr at Mar-26 from Rs 31.1 Cr at Mar-25.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition target] WFA, established 2001 and Mumbai-based, is a wealth management and financial distribution firm (investment advisory, mutual fund distribution, sub-broking) with a "25-year track record", 4,400+ total clients, 2,800+ client families, Assets Under Advisory of Rs 3,746 Cr and a team size of 25; its FY26 figures are given as Revenue 17.9, PAT 6.0, Networth 22.0 (Rs Cr).
- [Acquisition leadership] WFA's board includes Rakesh Mehta (MBA from JBIMS, "over 40 years of financial markets experience") and Nimesh Kenia (IIM Bangalore alumnus and Chartered Accountant, "25+ years of capital markets experience ... with Wealth First Advisors since 2001").
- [Regulatory] The company "Received SEBI approval to set up an AMC"; the journey slide records "With SEBI's formal license granted, Lakshya is now fully established and poised to commence operations", an IRDAI licence as a Direct Insurance Broker, and listing on BSE. One journey bullet also reads "The final SEBI inspection has been concluded, and approval is in its final stages".
- [Industry TAM] Deck cites Indian wealth management as "a $2.7 Tn Opportunity", with specialised wealth managers at "~11% of the total $2.7 Tn in serviceable assets", projected to rise to 17% share and grow AUM "from $300 billion to $1.6 trillion by FY35, representing a CAGR of approximately 18%", while serviceable assets grow from $2.7 trillion to "around $9.3 trillion at a CAGR of ~13%" (Source: Public Data, Broker Report).
- [Track record] Journey slide claims client-protection milestones: "Protected client wealth during Lehman crisis" and "Avoided NSEL scam - 100% client wealth protection"; earlier milestones include exclusive distribution for Franklin Templeton schemes and capturing "50% of Ahmedabad's retail MF market".
